```{r, include = FALSE}

  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 4

```

With staggered treatment adoption, the coefficient on the treatment indicator
from a two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression,

$$Y_{it} = \theta_t + \eta_i + \alpha D_{it} + e_{it},$$

is a weighted sum of group-time average treatment effects, $ATT(g,t)$, the
average effect for units first treated in period $g$ (group $g$) in period
$t$ (de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille, 2020; Goodman-Bacon, 2021). This
vignette shows how to recover those weights with `twfe_weights()`, and how to
compare them with the weights behind the overall average treatment effects of
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), from `attO_weights()` and
`att_simple_weights()`.

## Data and group-time average treatment effects

The example uses the county-level minimum wage data in the `did` package:
`lemp` is log teen employment, and `first.treat` is the year a county's state
first raised its minimum wage (0 for counties never treated in the sample).

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(twfeweights)
library(did)
data(mpdta, package = "did")
```

`twfe_weights()` takes the output of `did::att_gt()`. Two choices matter. The
comparison group must be the never-treated group, and the base period must be
`"universal"`: every $ATT(g,t)$, including pre-treatment ones, is then
measured relative to period $g-1$, which is what makes the TWFE decomposition
exact.

```{r}
attgt <- att_gt(
  yname = "lemp", tname = "year", idname = "countyreal",
  gname = "first.treat", data = mpdta,
  control_group = "nevertreated", base_period = "universal",
  bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE
)
```

## TWFE weights

```{r}
tw <- twfe_weights(attgt)
tw$weights_df
```

Each row is a group-time cell, with its TWFE weight, the estimated
$ATT(g,t)$, and whether the cell is post-treatment. The weighted sum of the
$ATT(g,t)$ reproduces the TWFE coefficient:

```{r}
sum(tw$weights_df$weight * tw$weights_df$attgt)

mpdta$D <- 1 * (mpdta$year >= mpdta$first.treat & mpdta$first.treat > 0)
coef(fixest::feols(lemp ~ D | countyreal + year, data = mpdta))
```

Three features of the weights are worth checking in any application.

**Post-treatment weights sum to one, but some can be negative.** Here the
cell for the 2004 group in 2007, its longest exposure, gets a negative
weight:

```{r}
post <- tw$weights_df$post == 1
sum(tw$weights_df$weight[post])
tw$weights_df[post & tw$weights_df$weight < 0, ]
```

**Pre-treatment cells get non-zero weight.** Under parallel trends (and no
anticipation), pre-treatment $ATT(g,t)$ are zero, so this part of the TWFE
estimate should be close to zero. When parallel trends fails in
pre-treatment periods, these terms feed directly into the TWFE estimate.

```{r}
c(
  post_part = sum(tw$weights_df$weight[post] * tw$weights_df$attgt[post]),
  pre_part = sum(tw$weights_df$weight[!post] * tw$weights_df$attgt[!post])
)
```

**The weights depend on the timing of treatment, not on how much each cell
matters for a target parameter.** `ggtwfeweights()` plots each cell's weight
against its $ATT(g,t)$:

```{r}
ggtwfeweights(tw)
```

## Weights behind overall average treatment effects

Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) propose combining the $ATT(g,t)$ with weights
chosen to target a specific parameter. `attO_weights()` gives the weights for
$ATT^o$, which averages each group's post-treatment effects and then averages
across groups by group size; `att_simple_weights()` gives the weights for
$ATT^{simple}$, which weights every post-treatment cell by group size, so
groups observed for more post-treatment periods count more. Both put zero
weight on pre-treatment cells, and their weights are non-negative.

```{r}
wo <- attO_weights(attgt)
ws <- att_simple_weights(attgt)

c(
  TWFE = sum(tw$weights_df$weight * tw$weights_df$attgt),
  ATT_o = sum(wo$weights_df$weight * wo$weights_df$attgt),
  ATT_simple = sum(ws$weights_df$weight * ws$weights_df$attgt)
)
```

These match the `"group"` and `"simple"` aggregations in `did::aggte()`:

```{r}
aggte(attgt, type = "group", bstrap = FALSE)$overall.att
aggte(attgt, type = "simple", bstrap = FALSE)$overall.att
```

Placing the weights side by side shows where the estimates differ: TWFE puts
less weight on long exposures, negative weight on some cells, and non-zero
weight on pre-treatment cells.

```{r}
comparison <- data.frame(
  group = tw$weights_df$group,
  time.period = tw$weights_df$time.period,
  post = tw$weights_df$post,
  attgt = tw$weights_df$attgt,
  TWFE = tw$weights_df$weight,
  ATT_o = wo$weights_df$weight,
  ATT_simple = ws$weights_df$weight
)
comparison[comparison$post == 1, ]
```

```{r}
ggtwfeweights(wo)
```

## Sampling weights

If `did::att_gt()` is called with `weightsname`, all three functions use the
same sampling weights by default, so `twfe_weights()` reproduces a weighted
TWFE regression (e.g., `fixest::feols(..., weights = ~w)`).

## References

Callaway, Brantly and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. "Difference-in-Differences with
Multiple Time Periods." *Journal of Econometrics* 225.2 (2021): 200-230.

de Chaisemartin, Clement and Xavier D'Haultfoeuille. "Two-Way Fixed Effects
Estimators with Heterogeneous Treatment Effects." *American Economic Review*
110.9 (2020): 2964-2996.

Goodman-Bacon, Andrew. "Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment
Timing." *Journal of Econometrics* 225.2 (2021): 254-277.
